This change passes an inline style object literal `{backgroundColor: theme.highlightBG, ...(!isLargeScreenWidth && {borderRadius: StyleUtils.getSearchTableHighlightBorderRadius(isLargeScreenWidth)})}` to the `pressableWrapperStyle` prop. Inline object literals allocate a new object every render (breaking memoization) and bypass the shared style system. This PR added `StyleUtils.getSearchRowBackgroundStyle` for exactly this background and applied it in the other list items, but this row inlines it instead.

Route the background through the shared helper and use a StyleUtils/`styles` token for the radius, e.g.:

```tsx
pressableWrapperStyle={[
    styles.mh5,
    StyleUtils.getSearchRowBackgroundStyle(isSelected),
    !isLargeScreenWidth && styles.componentBorderRadius, // or a StyleUtils radius helper
    isLargeScreenWidth && isLastItem && [styles.tableBottomRadius, styles.overflowHidden],
]}
```

This change passes an inline style object literal `{backgroundColor: theme.highlightBG, borderRadius: variables.componentBorderRadius}` to the `pressableWrapperStyle` prop. Inline object literals create a new object on every render (defeating memoization/reconciliation) and bypass the shared style system. Notably, this same PR added `StyleUtils.getSearchRowBackgroundStyle` and used it in every other list item (`ExpenseReportListItem`, `GroupChildrenContainer`, `GroupHeader`, `TransactionGroupListItem`, `TransactionListItem*`), so this row is inconsistent with the rest of the change.

Use the shared helper (and a `styles` token for the radius) instead of inlining the object:

```tsx
pressableWrapperStyle={[styles.mh5, StyleUtils.getSearchRowBackgroundStyle(isSelected), styles.componentBorderRadius]}
```

(add `const StyleUtils = useStyleUtils();` if not already present, and use the appropriate radius style token / StyleUtils helper rather than reading `variables.componentBorderRadius` inline).

Per `STYLING.md`, inline style object literals are not allowed. The `{height: variables.componentSizeLarge}` object is a static value that creates a new object every render and belongs in the shared style system. `variables.componentSizeLarge` is already used as a static `height` in many `styles` entries.

Add a reusable style (e.g. `styles.componentHeightLarge`) that sets `height: variables.componentSizeLarge` and reference it instead:

```tsx
<View style={[styles.w100, styles.justifyContentCenter, styles.componentHeightLarge]}>
    <LoadingIndicator iconSize={28} />
</View>
```

This passes an inline style object literal (`textStyles={{fontSize: variables.fontSizeSmall}}`) to a style-typed prop. Per `STYLING.md`, inline style objects are not allowed: they allocate a new object every render (breaking memoization), bypass theming, and duplicate a value that belongs in the shared style system. The value here is static (`variables.fontSizeSmall`) with no render-time computation, so it does not qualify for the dynamic-style exception.

Move it into `src/styles` (e.g. add a `styles.badgeTextCondensed` or similar helper) and pass the token instead. `Badge`'s `textStyles` prop is typed `StyleProp<TextStyle>`, so it accepts a shared style reference or array:

```tsx
<Badge
    text={translate('initialSettingsPage.troubleshoot.overridden')}
    isCondensed
    textStyles={styles.badgeTextCondensed}
    success
/>
```

This newly extracted `subtitleStyle` array uses an inline style object literal `{maxWidth: alternateTextMaxWidth}`. `StyleUtils` already exposes a helper for exactly this (`getMaximumWidth(maxWidth: number)` in `src/styles/utils/index.ts`), so the inline object bypasses the shared style system and allocates a fresh object each render.

Use the existing helper instead:

```tsx
const subtitleStyle = [
    isAlternateTextMultilineSupported && styles.preWrap,
    isAlternateTextMultilineSupported ? StyleUtils.getMaximumWidth(alternateTextMaxWidth) : null,
    isMultilineSupported ? StyleUtils.getPaddingLeft(paddingLeft) : null,
];
```

This changed line passes an inline style object literal to the `infoCellsTextStyle` (`*Style`) prop. Inline objects create a new object on every render (defeating memoization) and the hardcoded `lineHeight: 14` bypasses the shared style system. `14` is also a magic value that belongs in the style/`variables` layer.

Move the static value into `styles` and pass style tokens instead of an inline object, e.g. add a `lineHeight: 14` style helper and use:

```tsx
infoCellsTextStyle={[styles.textMicroBold, styles.lh14]}
```

This JSX passes an inline style object literal (`style={{width: variables.iconSizeMenuItem, height: variables.iconSizeMenuItem}}`) to a style-typed prop. Inline objects create a new object every render and bypass the shared style system. The values are static and belong in `styles`/`StyleUtils`.

Use a `StyleUtils` helper (or an array of `styles`) instead, for example:

```tsx
<View style={StyleUtils.getWidthAndHeightStyle(variables.iconSizeMenuItem, variables.iconSizeMenuItem)} />
```

This newly added `<View>` passes an inline style object literal `{height: variables.h40}`. `variables.h40` is a static value, so it belongs in the shared style system rather than an inline object created every render (which also breaks memoization). The same applies to the lone-View branch on line 63.

Add a helper/style entry (e.g. `styles.reportPreviewActionButtonRow` or a `StyleUtils` function returning `{height: variables.h40}`) and reference it:
```tsx
<View style={[buttonMaxWidth, styles.flex1, styles.flexRow, styles.gap2, styles.reportPreviewActionButtonHeight]}>
```

This passes an inline style object literal (`{backgroundColor: hovered ? theme.buttonHoveredBG : theme.buttonDefaultBG}`) to a style-typed prop. Inline style objects create a new object on every render (breaking memoization), bypass the shared style system, and are disallowed by `STYLING.md`. A `StyleUtils` helper already exists for exactly this case.

Use `StyleUtils.getBackgroundColorStyle(...)` instead:

```tsx
<View style={[styles.floatingActionButton, styles.floatingActionButtonSmall, StyleUtils.getBackgroundColorStyle(hovered ? theme.buttonHoveredBG : theme.buttonDefaultBG)]}>
```

This passes an inline object literal to a `style` prop. Inline style objects are disallowed per `STYLING.md`: they allocate a new object on every render (breaking memoization) and bypass the shared style system. The values here are static (a fixed `iconSizeNormal` square spacer), so they belong in the style helpers.

Use the existing `StyleUtils.getWidthAndHeightStyle` helper instead:

```tsx
<View style={StyleUtils.getWidthAndHeightStyle(variables.iconSizeNormal)} />
```

This passes an inline object literal to a `style` prop. Inline style objects are disallowed per `STYLING.md`: they allocate a new object on every render (breaking memoization) and bypass the shared style system. The values here are static (a fixed `iconSizeNormal` square spacer), so they belong in the style helpers.

Use the existing `StyleUtils.getWidthAndHeightStyle` helper instead:

```tsx
<View style={StyleUtils.getWidthAndHeightStyle(variables.iconSizeNormal)} />
```

This passes an inline style object literal (`{...styles.flexColumn, ...styles.alignItemsStretch}`) into the `wrapperStyle` array, which creates a new object every render and duplicates values that already exist as style tokens. Per `STYLING.md`, styles should come from `styles`/`StyleUtils` as array entries rather than inline object literals.

Add the existing tokens directly as array elements instead of spreading them into a new object:
```tsx
const listItemWrapperStyle = [styles.flex1, styles.userSelectNone, styles.flexColumn, styles.alignItemsStretch];
```

Per `STYLING.md`, inline style object literals are not allowed — they create a new object every render (breaking memoization) and bypass the shared style system. The value `{zIndex: 10}` already has a dedicated helper.

Replace the inline object with the existing `styles.zIndex10` helper (defined in `src/styles/index.ts`):

```tsx
return <View style={[StyleSheet.absoluteFill, styles.appBG, styles.zIndex10]}>{pickerScreen}</View>;
```

The `style={{width: SIZE, height: SIZE}}` and `webStyle={{width: SIZE, height: SIZE}}` props pass inline object literals to style-typed props. These are static values that belong in the shared style system and create a new object every render, breaking memoization.

Define a static style in `styles` (or via a `StyleUtils` sizing helper) and reference it, e.g. `style={styles.conciergeAnimatedAvatar}` / `webStyle={styles.conciergeAnimatedAvatar}`, instead of the inline objects.

This newly added JSX passes an inline style object literal `{width: variables.avatarSizeSubscript, height: variables.avatarSizeSubscript}` to a `style` prop. Inline object literals allocate a new object every render (defeating memoization) and keep static dimensions out of the shared style system.

Move this to a named style in `styles`/`StyleUtils` (or a `StyleUtils.getWidthAndHeightStyle(...)`-style helper) and reference it, e.g. `style={[styles.moneyRequestAttachReceiptThumbnailIcon, styles.receiptPlaceholderPlusIconSubscript]}`, so the size values live in the style system rather than inline in the component.

The modified `innerStyles` array still passes an inline style object literal `{maxWidth: 256}` to a style-typed prop. Per `STYLING.md`, inline style objects are disallowed: they allocate a new object every render (breaking memoization), bypass theming, and hardcode a value that belongs in the shared style system. Since this PR is specifically restoring the `256px` cap as the effective max width, this is a good opportunity to move it into the style system rather than leave it inline.

Add a reusable helper to `src/styles/index.ts` (e.g. `maxWidthFilterPill: {maxWidth: 256}` or use a `variables` entry) and reference it instead:

```tsx
innerStyles={[isExpanded && styles.buttonHoveredBG, styles.maxWidthFilterPill, styles.flexShrink1, innerStyles, shouldShowCloseButton && styles.pr2]}
```

An inline style object literal (`{textAlign}`) is passed to `style`. `textAlign` here is one of only three fixed values (`left`/`center`/`right`) and equivalent helpers already exist in the style system (`styles.textAlignCenter`, `styles.textAlignRight`), so this should not be an inline object.

Use the existing named styles selected conditionally rather than an inline object:

```tsx
const textAlignStyle = isRight ? styles.textAlignRight : isCenter ? styles.textAlignCenter : undefined;
// ...
<Text style={[isHeaderCell ? styles.htmlTableHeaderCellText : styles.htmlTableCellText, textAlignStyle]}>
```

An inline style object literal (`{alignItems}`) is passed to `style`. Inline objects create a new object on every render (breaking memoization) and bypass the shared style system. `alignItems` here is one of only three fixed values (`flex-start`/`center`/`flex-end`), not a genuinely dynamic measured dimension, and equivalent helpers already exist (`styles.alignItemsStart`/`styles.alignItemsCenter`/`styles.alignItemsEnd`).

Select the appropriate named style instead of building an inline object. For example, have `getCellAlignment` return a style reference:

```tsx
const alignmentStyle = isRight ? styles.alignItemsEnd : isCenter ? styles.alignItemsCenter : styles.alignItemsStart;
// ...
<View style={[styles.htmlTableCell, alignmentStyle]}>
```

This passes an inline style object literal to the `style` prop. Per `STYLING.md`, inline style objects are not allowed—they allocate a new object every render and bypass the shared style system. Although `scale`/`designWidth`/`designHeight` are dynamic, `transformOrigin: 'top left'` is static and the width/height have a dedicated `StyleUtils` helper.

Move the static/dimension values into the style system, e.g. combine `StyleUtils.getWidthAndHeightStyle(designWidth, designHeight)` with a shared style for `transformOrigin`, and keep only the truly dynamic `transform: [{scale}]` computed inline via a `StyleUtils` function:

```tsx
<View style={[StyleUtils.getWidthAndHeightStyle(designWidth, designHeight), styles.transformOriginTopLeft, StyleUtils.getTransformScaleStyle(scale)]}>
```

This passes an inline style object literal to the `style` prop. Per `STYLING.md`, inline style objects are not allowed: they allocate a new object every render and bypass the shared style system. While the width/height here are genuinely dynamic, `overflow: 'hidden'` is a static value with an existing helper (`styles.overflowHidden`), and the dynamic dimensions have a dedicated `StyleUtils` helper.

Use `StyleUtils.getWidthAndHeightStyle` for the computed dimensions and `styles.overflowHidden` for the static part:

```tsx
const StyleUtils = useStyleUtils();
// ...
<View style={[StyleUtils.getWidthAndHeightStyle(designWidth * scale, designHeight * scale), styles.overflowHidden]}>
```

This line passes an inline style object literal (`style={{maxWidth: variables.tabSelectorMaxTabLabelWidth, flexShrink: 1, minWidth: 0}}`) to a style-typed prop. Per `STYLING.md`, inline style objects are not allowed: they allocate a new object on every render (defeating memoization) and duplicate values that belong in the shared style system. This change compounds the issue by adding two more static values (`flexShrink: 1`, `minWidth: 0`) inline.

Move these static values into the shared `styles` object (e.g. a `styles.tabSelectorLabelContainer` entry combining `maxWidth`, `flexShrink: 1`, `minWidth: 0`) and reference it:

```tsx
<View style={styles.tabSelectorLabelContainer}>
```

Define the style once in `src/styles/index.ts` rather than inline in JSX.

This passes an inline object literal `{height: PROMPT_MAX_HEIGHT_ON_KEYBOARD_OPEN_LANDSCAPE_MODE}` to the `style` prop. Per `STYLING.md`, inline style object literals are not allowed — they allocate a new object on every render (breaking memoization) and bypass the shared style system. The value is a static module-level constant, so use the dedicated `StyleUtils` helper.

Replace the inline object with `StyleUtils.getHeight`:

```tsx
<View style={shouldShrinkPromptInput ? StyleUtils.getHeight(PROMPT_MAX_HEIGHT_ON_KEYBOARD_OPEN_LANDSCAPE_MODE) : [styles.flex1]}>
```

(`StyleUtils` comes from `useStyleUtils()`.)

This passes an inline object literal `{height: PROMPT_MAX_HEIGHT_ON_KEYBOARD_OPEN_LANDSCAPE_MODE}` to the `style` prop. Per `STYLING.md`, inline style object literals are not allowed — they create a new object on every render (breaking memoization) and bypass the shared style system. The value here is a static module-level constant, so there is a `StyleUtils` helper that fits exactly.

Use the existing `StyleUtils.getHeight` helper instead:

```tsx
<View style={shouldShrinkPromptInput ? StyleUtils.getHeight(PROMPT_MAX_HEIGHT_ON_KEYBOARD_OPEN_LANDSCAPE_MODE) : [shouldUseScrollableLayout ? styles.h42 : styles.flex1]}>
```

(`StyleUtils` comes from `useStyleUtils()`.)

This line passes an inline object literal `{minHeight: itemHeight ?? variables.optionRowHeightCompact}` into the `listItemWrapperStyle` style array. Inline style objects create a new object every render (breaking memoization) and bypass the shared style system. A dedicated `StyleUtils` helper already exists for exactly this case (`getMinimumHeight(minHeight: number)` in `src/styles/utils/index.ts`), and it's already used elsewhere in this same `FilterComponents` directory (e.g. `AmountFilterContent.tsx`).

Replace the inline object with the helper:

```tsx
const StyleUtils = useStyleUtils();
// ...
listItemWrapperStyle: [StyleUtils.getMinimumHeight(itemHeight ?? variables.optionRowHeightCompact), selectionListStyle?.listItemWrapperStyle],
```

The `style` array passes an inline object literal `{minHeight: CONST.POPOVER_REPORT_SUBMIT_TO_CONTENT_HEIGHT}`. Per `STYLING.md`, inline style objects are not allowed and a `StyleUtils` helper already exists for this static value.

Use `StyleUtils.getMinimumHeight` instead:
```tsx
<View style={[styles.w100, styles.flex1, styles.pt3, styles.pb3, !isBottomDockedInLandscape && StyleUtils.getMinimumHeight(CONST.POPOVER_REPORT_SUBMIT_TO_CONTENT_HEIGHT)]}>
```

The `innerContainerStyle` prop is passed an inline object literal containing static style values (`{width: CONST.POPOVER_DROPDOWN_WIDTH}` and `{minHeight: popoverDimensions.minHeight}`). Per `STYLING.md`, inline style objects are not allowed — they create a new object every render and bypass the shared style system. These static values have direct `StyleUtils` helpers.

Replace the inline literals with `StyleUtils` helpers, e.g.:
```tsx
innerContainerStyle={[
    isSmallScreenWidth ? styles.w100 : StyleUtils.getWidthStyle(CONST.POPOVER_DROPDOWN_WIDTH),
    isBottomDockedInLandscape ? styles.getPopoverMaxHeight(windowHeight, true) : StyleUtils.getMinimumHeight(popoverDimensions.minHeight),
]}
```

Per `STYLING.md`, inline style object literals (`style={{ ... }}`) are not allowed. The inline `{width: '100%', height: '100%'}` object is created on every render and duplicates static values that already exist in the shared style system as `styles.w100` and `styles.h100`.

Replace the inline object with the shared helpers:

```tsx
<Image
    source={source}
    style={[styles.w100, styles.h100]}
    resizeMode="cover"
    accessibilityIgnoresInvertColors
/>
```

Per `STYLING.md`, inline style object literals (`style={{ ... }}`) are not allowed. The inline `{flex: 1}` object is created on every render (breaking memoization) and duplicates a value that already exists in the shared style system. A direct equivalent (`styles.flex1`) is available. Note the existing `EReceiptThumbnail` component uses `styles.flex1` here.

Add `const styles = useThemeStyles();` and replace the inline object:

```tsx
const styles = useThemeStyles();
// ...
<View style={[styles.flex1, style]}>
```

This `<View>` passes an inline style object literal (`{width: size, height: size, borderRadius: size / 2, backgroundColor: colors.backgroundColor}`) to the `style` prop. Per `STYLING.md`, inline style objects are not allowed — they allocate a new object every render and bypass the shared style system. Equivalent `StyleUtils` helpers already exist for every value here.

Use the `StyleUtils` helpers instead of an inline object, e.g.:
```tsx
const StyleUtils = useStyleUtils();
// ...
<View
    style={[
        styles.circle,
        StyleUtils.getWidthAndHeightStyle(size, size),
        StyleUtils.getBorderRadiusStyle(size / 2),
        StyleUtils.getBackgroundColorStyle(colors.backgroundColor),
    ]}
>
```

Inline style object literals (`{top: 8, right: 8}` and `{top: 4, right: 4}`) are passed to the `style` prop. Per `STYLING.md`, inline style objects are not allowed: they allocate a new object every render (breaking memoization), bypass theming, and duplicate spacing values that belong in the shared style system. These are static spacing values, not render-time computed dimensions.

Move these to the shared `styles` system (e.g. add `styles.codeBlockCopyButtonWrapper` / `styles.codeBlockCopyButtonWrapperMultiline`, or a `StyleUtils.getCodeBlockCopyButtonStyle(isMultilineCodeBlock)` helper) and reference them instead:

```tsx
<View style={[styles.pAbsolute, StyleUtils.getCodeBlockCopyButtonStyle(isMultilineCodeBlock)]}>
```

This style array passes an inline style object literal `{zIndex: 1}`, which is disallowed per `STYLING.md`. Inline objects create a new object every render (breaking memoization) and duplicate values that belong in the style system. A direct equivalent already exists: `styles.zIndex1`.

Replace the inline object with the existing style helper:

```tsx
<View style={[styles.pAbsolute, styles.p5, styles.t0, styles.l0, styles.zIndex1]}>
```

`innerContainerStyle={!shouldUseNarrowLayout ? {maxWidth: variables.modalContentMaxWidth} : undefined}` passes an inline style object literal to a `*Style` prop. `{maxWidth: variables.modalContentMaxWidth}` is a fully static value that belongs in the shared style system; the inline literal creates a new object every render and bypasses the styles helpers.

Add a named style (e.g. `styles.popoverMaxWidth` returning `{maxWidth: variables.modalContentMaxWidth}`) in the style sheet and reference it: `innerContainerStyle={!shouldUseNarrowLayout ? styles.popoverMaxWidth : undefined}`.

The `iconStyles={{borderRadius: variables.componentBorderRadiusNormal}}` prop receives an inline style object literal, which is disallowed by `STYLING.md`. Inline objects create a new object every render (breaking memoization) and bypass the shared style system.

Use a shared style from `styles` (or a `StyleUtils` helper) instead of an inline object, e.g.:

```tsx
iconStyles={[styles.br3]}
```

(Pick the existing border-radius style token that maps to `componentBorderRadiusNormal`, or add one to the style system if missing.)

This `style` array passes an inline object literal `{color: theme.textSupporting}`. Per `STYLING.md`, inline style objects are not allowed — they allocate a new object every render and bypass the shared style system. An equivalent already exists: the `styles.textSupporting` named style (and `StyleUtils.getTextColorStyle(...)`).

Use the existing named style instead of the inline object:

```tsx
<Text style={[styles.buttonSmallText, styles.textSupporting]}>{label}</Text>
```

This `style` array passes an inline object literal `{minHeight: variables.componentSizeSmall}`. Per `STYLING.md`, inline style object literals are not allowed — they create a new object on every render (breaking memoization) and duplicate values that belong in the style system. `minHeight` here is a static value derived from `variables`, so it belongs in the shared `styles`/`StyleUtils`.

Replace the inline object with a named style (or a `StyleUtils` helper). For example, add a `minHeightComponentSizeSmall` (or equivalent) entry to `styles` and use it:

```tsx
<View style={[styles.flexRow, styles.alignItemsCenter, styles.justifyContentCenter, styles.minHeightComponentSizeSmall]}>
```
